citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
The facility did not use the appropriate methods to prevent, control, diagnose, and treat an injury in a Yorkie female (dog
#012). The dog was evaluated on October 8, 2026, for an injury. The veterinarian prescribed an anti-inflammatory pain
medication (Previcox) to be given for three days. The medical records were obtained from the veterinarian’s office. The
facility did not administer any doses of the prescribed medication.
APHIS inspectors assess that adequate veterinary care is being provided to dogs at licensed facilities. Facilities must
ensure medications prescribed by the veterinarian are given to provide treatment for injuries. Lack of or delay in treatment
may prolong pain or stress for the dog. Correct by ensuring the usage of appropriate methods to prevent, control,
diagnose, and treat an injury in an animal, and the availability of emergency, weekend, and holiday care. Correct by:
October 14, 2026, onward.

citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
The facility did not communicate to the veterinarian a serious medical condition for Dog #012 in a timely manner. Female
Yorkie Dog #012 was identified by the APHIS inspector on Oct 1, 2026, as having an injury caused by a chain collar. The
facility was instructed to have the dog evaluated by a veterinarian by noon on October 3, 2026. The dog was not
evaluated by a veterinarian until October 8, 2026.
Failure to have a mechanism of direct and frequent communication with the veterinarian so that timely and accurate
information on problems of animal health, behavior, and well-being being conveyed to the attending veterinarian can lead
to worsening of medical conditions, delay in proper diagnosis and treatment, and may result in unnecessary pain and
distress to the animals. Correct by ensuring timely, direct, and frequent communication with the veterinarian in instances
of injury, diseases, or illness.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the licensee.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
